**Comparison: John S. vs. Brian K.** (two freelancers with the most front-end-relevant profiles on evals-topwork.vercel.app)  I chose these two because John's profile is explicitly front-end, and Brian is the other developer profile in the "Your hires" list. The site has no front-end filter, and the Talent tab returned a 404, so I couldn't browse further. Carol A. (UI/UX) and Alexa R. (Full Stack) were not profiled.  | | **John S.** (New York) | **Brian K.** (Toronto) | |---|---|---| | Title | Full Stack Developer, with frontend history | Full-Stack Developer, backend-leaning | | Earnings / jobs / hours | $30k+ / 35 / 900 | $12k+ / 18 / 450 | | Listed reviews | 4.9 (SaaS platform, $120/hr, 160 hrs); 4.8 (frontend e-commerce, $115/hr, 170 hrs) | 4.9 (e-commerce, $75/hr, 120 hrs); 4.8 (backend financial app, $70/hr, 100 hrs) | | Core skills | JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Redux, Node, GraphQL, Docker, AWS | JavaScript, Vue.js, Node, Express, MongoDB, GraphQL, Docker, AWS, Kubernetes, CI/CD | | Work history | Frontend Developer at Creative Web Agency (2013–18); Full Stack at Innovative Tech Solutions (2018–present) | Backend Developer at Creative Solutions (2015–18); Full-Stack at Tech Innovators (2018–present) | | Verification | ID verified | ID verified |  **John S.** - Pros: Stronger front-end signal (React/Redux/TypeScript, and a frontend role in his history). Higher volume (35 jobs, 900 hours). Both reviews are 4.8 or higher, and the feedback names frontend quality and on-schedule delivery. - Cons: Higher rate ($115–120/hr). Only two reviews are shown, so the sample is small. Feedback is brief.  **Brian K.** - Pros: Lower rate ($70–75/hr). Strong on backend, CI/CD and Kubernetes. Both reviews are 4.8 or higher. - Cons: Smaller track record (18 jobs, 450 hours). Less explicit front-end experience; the feedback praises backend work, and the e-commerce review mentions frontend only in passing. Profile data is inconsistent: the dashboard lists him at $15.00/hr with a 4.5 rating and 120 reviews, while his profile shows $75/hr and 4.9/4.8 on two projects. The reviews also refer to him as "David," not "Brian."  **Caveats** - The site shows no explicit job success rate. I used completed-job count and review scores as proxies. - Neither profile has a review history beyond the two shown.  **Recommendation:** For front-end work, John S. is the stronger fit, at a higher price. Brian K. is a cheaper full-stack option, but confirm his rate and rating before hiring, given the mismatch on the dashboard.

I could not find a dedicated front-end freelancer listing. The site's Talent menu opens a submenu that doesn't respond to clicks, and the search box doesn't return results. So I compared the two profiles closest to front-end work from the dashboard. Neither is labeled "front-end," and neither profile shows a job success rate.  **Brian K.** (Toronto; full-stack, Vue.js and Node.js) - **Work history:** 18 jobs, $12k+ earned, 450 hours, works more than 40 hrs/week, ID verified, about 6 years of experience. - **Client feedback:** 4.9 on an e-commerce build ($9,000, 120 hrs) and 4.8 on a financial-app backend ($7,000, 100 hrs). Both reviews praise delivery on time and quality. - **Pros:** Largest and most substantial track record of the two, with proven large projects. - **Cons:** Full-stack rather than front-end focused. Rates conflict: $75/hr on the profile versus $15/hr on the dashboard card. The dashboard card also shows a 4.5 rating, while the profile reviews are 4.9 and 4.8.  **Alexa R.** (Mosquera, Colombia; full-stack with React focus) - **Work history:** 4 jobs, $2k+ earned, 100 hours, more than 30 hrs/week, ID verified, web development since 2014. - **Client feedback:** Three 5-star-range reviews (5, 4.8, 5) on a $500 Squarespace job, a $3,000 e-commerce build, and a $2,200 backend job. - **Pros:** Stronger front-end skill set (React, TypeScript, Material-UI, Bootstrap, Jest, Cypress). Lower rate, $50/hr. - **Cons:** Much thinner history, with only 4 jobs and 100 hours on the profile. The dashboard card shows 120 jobs, which contradicts the profile. Reviews are short-project and only three.  **Bottom line:** Brian K. is the safer hire for substantial work based on the volume and review history. Alexa R. fits a front-end-specific need better, but with less evidence behind it. Verify rates and job counts before hiring, since the cards and profiles disagree for both.
